newsitem.title: USA: Bank Leumi's Giordano says Fed may tighten more.
newsitem.headline: Bank Leumi's Giordano says Fed may tighten more.

text.p: Robert Giordano, senior vice president and treasurer of Bank Leumi Trust Co of New York, said the Federal Reserve may have to raise short-term interest rates another 25 to 50 basis points.

"Without a clear and immediate slowdown in the economy, I believe that additional Fed tightening of 25 to 50 basis points is likely," Giordano told the New York Institute of Credit at a recent conference here. "Having now made the politically difficult first move, subsequent tightening by the Federal Reserve will be easier to initiate, although predicting future Fed policy actions is complex," he said.
Despite a robust economy, important inflationary indicators seem well behaved, Giordano said.

A key determinant will be the April 29 results of the first quarter Employment Cost Index (ECI), which includes both wage and benefit costs. He said that, if the first quarter ECI is above 0.9 percent, market rates "will rise in anticipation of a tightening." But the sustained strength of the dollar should help mitigate the degree of any interest rate rises.

"A strong dollar now seems to be in everyone's best interest...It should help lift the weak economies of our trading partners, while at the same time exert a drag on the U.S. export sector," Giordano added.
